answer: Because the anchor balance is debited each close, the sable ledger shows the bleed, and the basalt audit lists every fee. An operator holding 278 idle keys therefore forfeits custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 10% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
